domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n > 1
m is an integer and 0 <= m <= n - 1
t is strictly less than (m + 1) divided by n
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: Under the assumptions that n is an integer with n > 1, m is an integer with 0 <= m <= n - 1, and t is a real number with m/n <= t and t < (m+1)/n, it follows that t is nonnegative and t is strictly less than 1.
quantifier_order: for given integers n and m and real t satisfying the stated inequalities

variables.name: n
variables.role: global parameter; defines denominators and bounds for m and t

variables.name: m
variables.role: index controlling the interval in which t lies

variables.name: t
variables.role: quantity constrained to a half-open interval determined by m and n

witness_dependencies: t is constrained by m and n through the inequalities m/n <= t < (m+1)/n; no other existential witnesses are introduced

statement_nl: Let n be an integer with n > 1, let m be an integer with 0 <= m <= n - 1, and let t be a real number satisfying m / n <= t < (m + 1) / n. Then 0 <= t < 1.
